issues.detail: The Greek 'εαν δε και' (ean de kai) functions as a conditional/concessive structure roughly meaning 'even if' or 'even though'. The Vietnamese translation 'Nếu... cũng sẽ' (If... also will) changes the logical relationship from a concession of a hypothetical situation to a certain future result.

The Greek 'αποκριθητε' and 'απολυσητε' are in the Aorist Imperative (commands/requests). The Vietnamese translation uses the Future Tense ('sẽ không'), which changes the mood from a request/command to a prediction of future action.
